summary.text: John Morley, III is a Republican state senator from the Orleans District who was appointed by Governor Phil Scott on December 5, 2025, to replace Samuel Douglass, and is seeking re-election on both the Republican and Democratic lines.
He previously served in the Vermont House of Representatives from 2005 to 2010 and worked as a lineman and as village manager of Orleans.

paragraphs.text: John Morley, III earned a high school diploma from Lake Region Union High School and a bachelor's degree from the University of Vermont, according to Ballotpedia.
His career includes work as a lineman and service as Village Manager and an elected Trustee for the Village of Orleans.

Ballotpedia lists his affiliations as the Vermont Public Power Supply Authority, the Northeast Public Power Association, the Northeastern Vermont Development Association, and Orleans/Essex VNA and Hospice.
Morley represented the Orleans-Caledonia District in the Vermont House from 2005 to 2010 and served on the Appropriations and Energy committees, and he did not run for re-election in 2010.
Governor Phil Scott appointed him to the State Senate on December 5, 2025, and his current term ends in January 2027.
He won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary and advanced from the Democratic primary as a write-in candidate.
